opener: Father, some mornings I wake up and nothing in my life looks finished — no shape yet, no clear direction, just waiting, and I don't know how to pray about that except to bring You the waiting itself.
paragraphs: I think about how it was before anything existed — dark, empty, nothing holding together — and then You spoke, and the world took shape. I need You to do that again in me. The relationship I can't fix on my own, the job that still hasn't opened up, the dream that's gone quiet for a season — none of it looks like much right now, but it was never going to look like much before You spoke over it. So I'm not asking You to explain the silence. I'm asking You to speak into it.

I declare today that the darkness pressing in on me — the doubt, the comparison, the fear that I'm being left behind while everyone else's life seems to be moving — is no match for You. You are the Word who was there before anything was made, and here is the truth I am holding onto this morning: darkness has never once put out Your light. You are not finished making something out of me. Hold me steady while I wait on the rest of the sentence You are still writing over my life. In Jesus' name, amen.
bold: darkness has never once put out Your light
footerNote: Save this & send it to someone still waiting on their shape to show
